- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

163		rssHeading, err := getRSSHeading(ctx, s.Store)
164		if err != nil {
165			return "", time.Time{}, err
166		}
167	
168		feed := &feeds.Feed{
169			Title:       rssHeading.Title,
170			Link:        &feeds.Link{Href: baseURL},
171			Description: rssHeading.Description,
172			Created:     time.Now(),
173		}
174	
175		var itemCountLimit = min(len(memoList), maxRSSItemCount)
176		if itemCountLimit == 0 {
177			// Return empty feed if no memos
178			rss, err := feed.ToRss()
179			return rss, time.Time{}, err
180		}
181	
182		// Track the most recent update time for Last-Modified header
183		var lastModified time.Time

185			lastModified = time.Unix(memoList[0].UpdatedTs, 0)
186		}
187	
188		// Batch load all attachments for all memos to avoid N+1 query problem

207		for {

211			case <-c.stopChan:

217	// cleanup removes expired items.
218	func (c *Cache) cleanup() {
219		evicted := make(map[string]any)
220		count := 0
221	
222		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
223			itm, ok := value.(item)
224			if !ok {
225				return true
226			}
227			if time.Now().After(itm.expiration) {
228				c.data.Delete(key)
229				count++
230	
231				if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
232					if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok {
233						evicted[keyStr] = itm.value
234					}
235				}
236			}
237			return true
238		})
239	
240		if count > 0 {
241			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(count))
242	
243			// Call eviction callbacks outside the loop to avoid blocking the range
244			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
245				for k, v := range evicted {
246					c.config.OnEviction(k, v)
247				}
248			}
249		}
250	}

252	// cleanupOldest removes the oldest items if we're over the max items.
253	func (c *Cache) cleanupOldest() {
254		// Remove 20% of max items at once
255		threshold := max(c.config.MaxItems/5, 1)
256	
257		currentCount := (&c.itemCount).Load()
258	
259		// If we're not over the threshold, don't do anything
260		if currentCount <= int64(c.config.MaxItems) {
261			return
262		}
263	
264		// Find the oldest items
265		type keyExpPair struct {
266			key        string
267			value      any
268			expiration time.Time
269		}
270		candidates := make([]keyExpPair, 0, threshold)
271	
272		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
273			itm, ok := value.(item)
274			if !ok {
275				return true
276			}
277			if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok && len(candidates) < threshold {
278				candidates = append(candidates, keyExpPair{keyStr, itm.value, itm.expiration})
279				return true
280			}
281	
282			// Find the newest item in candidates
283			newestIdx := 0
284			for i := 1; i < len(candidates); i++ {
285				if candidates[i].expiration.After(candidates[newestIdx].expiration) {
286					newestIdx = i
287				}
288			}
289	
290			// Replace it if this item is older
291			if itm.expiration.Before(candidates[newestIdx].expiration) {
292				candidates[newestIdx] = keyExpPair{key.(string), itm.value, itm.expiration}
293			}
294	
295			return true
296		})
297	
298		// Delete the oldest items
299		deletedCount := 0
300		for _, candidate := range candidates {
301			c.data.Delete(candidate.key)
302			deletedCount++
303	
304			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
305				c.config.OnEviction(candidate.key, candidate.value)
306			}
307		}
308	
309		// Update count
310		if deletedCount > 0 {
311			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(deletedCount))
312		}
313	}

322		case map[string]any:
323			return len(v) * 64 // rough estimate
324		default:
325			return 64 // default conservative estimate

66	// Cache is a thread-safe in-memory cache with TTL and memory management.
67	type Cache struct {
68		itemCount  atomic.Int64 // Use atomic operations to track item count
69		data       sync.Map
70		config     Config
71		stopChan   chan struct{}
72		closedChan chan struct{}
73	}
74	
75	// New creates a new memory cache with the given configuration.
76	func New(config Config) *Cache {
77		c := &Cache{
78			config:     config,
79			stopChan:   make(chan struct{}),
80			closedChan: make(chan struct{}),
81		}
82	
83		go c.cleanupLoop()
84		return c
85	}
86	
87	// NewDefault creates a new memory cache with default configuration.
88	func NewDefault() *Cache {
89		return New(DefaultConfig())
90	}

92	// Set adds a value to the cache with the default TTL.
93	func (c *Cache) Set(ctx context.Context, key string, value any) {
94		c.SetWithTTL(ctx, key, value, c.config.DefaultTTL)
95	}
96	
97	// SetWithTTL adds a value to the cache with a custom TTL.
98	func (c *Cache) SetWithTTL(_ context.Context, key string, value any, ttl time.Duration) {
99		// Estimate size of the item (very rough approximation).
100		size := estimateSize(value)
101	
102		// Check if item already exists to avoid double counting.
103		if _, exists := c.data.Load(key); exists {
104			c.data.Delete(key)
105		} else {
106			// Only increment if this is a new key.
107			(&c.itemCount).Add(1)
108		}
109	
110		c.data.Store(key, item{
111			value:      value,
112			expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl),
113			size:       size,
114		})
115	
116		// If we're over the max items, clean up old items.
117		if c.config.MaxItems > 0 && (&c.itemCount).Load() > int64(c.config.MaxItems) {
118			c.cleanupOldest()
119		}
120	}

122	// Get retrieves a value from the cache.
123	func (c *Cache) Get(_ context.Context, key string) (any, bool) {
124		value, ok := c.data.Load(key)
125		if !ok {
126			return nil, false
127		}
128	
129		itm, ok := value.(item)
130		if !ok {
131			// If the value is not of type item, it means it was corrupted or not set correctly.
132			c.data.Delete(key)
133			return nil, false
134		}
135		if time.Now().After(itm.expiration) {
136			c.data.Delete(key)
137			(&c.itemCount).Add(-1)
138	
139			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
140				c.config.OnEviction(key, itm.value)
141			}
142	
143			return nil, false
144		}
145	
146		return itm.value, true
147	}

149	// Delete removes a value from the cache.
150	func (c *Cache) Delete(_ context.Context, key string) {
151		if value, loaded := c.data.LoadAndDelete(key); loaded {
152			(&c.itemCount).Add(-1)
153	
154			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
155				if itm, ok := value.(item); ok {
156					c.config.OnEviction(key, itm.value)
157				}
158			}
159		}
160	}

162	// Clear removes all values from the cache.
163	func (c *Cache) Clear(_ context.Context) {
164		count := 0
165		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
166			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
167				itm, ok := value.(item)
168				if ok {
169					if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok {
170						c.config.OnEviction(keyStr, itm.value)
171					}
172				}
173			}
174			c.data.Delete(key)
175			count++
176			return true
177		})
178		(&c.itemCount).Store(0)
179	}

182	func (c *Cache) Size() int64 {

186	// Close stops the cache cleanup goroutine.
187	func (c *Cache) Close() error {
188		select {
189		case <-c.stopChan:
190			// Already closed
191			return nil
192		default:
193			close(c.stopChan)
194			<-c.closedChan // Wait for cleanup goroutine to exit
195			return nil
196		}
197	}

199	// cleanupLoop periodically cleans up expired items.
200	func (c *Cache) cleanupLoop() {
201		ticker := time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)
202		defer func() {
203			ticker.Stop()
204			close(c.closedChan)
205		}()
206	
207		for {
208			select {
209			case <-ticker.C:
210				c.cleanup()
211			case <-c.stopChan:
212				return
213			}
214		}
215	}

217	// cleanup removes expired items.
218	func (c *Cache) cleanup() {
219		evicted := make(map[string]any)
220		count := 0
221	
222		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
223			itm, ok := value.(item)
224			if !ok {
225				return true
226			}
227			if time.Now().After(itm.expiration) {
228				c.data.Delete(key)
229				count++
230	
231				if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
232					if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok {
233						evicted[keyStr] = itm.value
234					}
235				}
236			}
237			return true
238		})
239	
240		if count > 0 {
241			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(count))
242	
243			// Call eviction callbacks outside the loop to avoid blocking the range
244			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
245				for k, v := range evicted {
246					c.config.OnEviction(k, v)
247				}
248			}
249		}
250	}

252	// cleanupOldest removes the oldest items if we're over the max items.
253	func (c *Cache) cleanupOldest() {
254		// Remove 20% of max items at once
255		threshold := max(c.config.MaxItems/5, 1)
256	
257		currentCount := (&c.itemCount).Load()
258	
259		// If we're not over the threshold, don't do anything
260		if currentCount <= int64(c.config.MaxItems) {
261			return
262		}
263	
264		// Find the oldest items
265		type keyExpPair struct {
266			key        string
267			value      any
268			expiration time.Time
269		}
270		candidates := make([]keyExpPair, 0, threshold)
271	
272		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
273			itm, ok := value.(item)
274			if !ok {
275				return true
276			}
277			if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok && len(candidates) < threshold {
278				candidates = append(candidates, keyExpPair{keyStr, itm.value, itm.expiration})
279				return true
280			}
281	
282			// Find the newest item in candidates
283			newestIdx := 0
284			for i := 1; i < len(candidates); i++ {
285				if candidates[i].expiration.After(candidates[newestIdx].expiration) {
286					newestIdx = i
287				}
288			}
289	
290			// Replace it if this item is older
291			if itm.expiration.Before(candidates[newestIdx].expiration) {
292				candidates[newestIdx] = keyExpPair{key.(string), itm.value, itm.expiration}
293			}
294	
295			return true
296		})
297	
298		// Delete the oldest items
299		deletedCount := 0
300		for _, candidate := range candidates {
301			c.data.Delete(candidate.key)
302			deletedCount++
303	
304			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
305				c.config.OnEviction(candidate.key, candidate.value)
306			}
307		}
308	
309		// Update count
310		if deletedCount > 0 {
311			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(deletedCount))
312		}
313	}

315	// estimateSize attempts to estimate the memory footprint of a value.
316	func estimateSize(value any) int {
317		switch v := value.(type) {
318		case string:
319			return len(v) + 24 // base size + string overhead
320		case []byte:
321			return len(v) + 24 // base size + slice overhead
322		case map[string]any:
323			return len(v) * 64 // rough estimate
324		default:
325			return 64 // default conservative estimate
326		}
327	}
